A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLForensics. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, allowing relocated material and substantive differences to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across five datasets, including baseline comparisons, ablations and adaptive attacks in Tables 3–14.

after.justification: v2 retains the work's original experimental results, including the five-dataset comparisons in Table 2 and adaptive-attack evaluations in Figure 4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same two influence scores, checkpoint calculations, scaled HDBSCAN clustering and cluster/outlier decision rules. The centralized-learning and target-input detection adaptations already appear in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, MNIST, Sentiment140 and ImageNet-Fruits. Clean-label attacks, adaptive attacks and centralized learning on imbalanced CIFAR-10 also appear in both; their relocation does not add coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain PF, FLForensics-G, FLForensics-A, FLDetector and the same aggregation defenses. Newly cited attack and defense papers are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Matched experiments retain their splits, architectures, training budgets, metrics, attack parameters and checkpoint procedures; v1 Table 16 matches v2 Table 5. Newly disclosed implementation details and omission of the default non-iid value do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: v1 Table 13's additional analysis of FLForensics under ALIE and Edge attacks with Trim, Median, FLTrust and FLAME is omitted. Other sensitivity studies, adaptive attacks, recovery experiments and supplementary case studies are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's checklist acknowledges the absence of formal error bars but adds no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The main comparison and retained appendix tables preserve their numerical results. However, v1 Table 13's detection results disappear, and v2 Figure 4 plots an FNR of approximately 0.116 for attacking every 10 rounds, versus 0.000 in v1 Table 11a, while retaining DACC 0.900 and FPR 0.125.

T1.justification: The formal definition, assumptions, three theorems, Corollary 1 and their proofs are retained in v2 Appendix B. The added Corollary 2 repeats the existing influence-score ratio inequality rather than introducing a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: the first FL poison-forensics method, theoretical justification under stated assumptions, and empirical effectiveness across five datasets against existing and adaptive attacks.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 8's explicit privacy warning about checkpoint exposure following a server compromise. Appendix I also softens the untargeted-attack limitation from 'ineffective' to 'less effective'; the new checklist claims statistical robustness from experimental breadth without additional statistical evidence.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies MXNet, a Quadro RTX 6000 GPU with 24GB memory, dataset access/licensing information and a code/data link. It omits v1's explicit default non-iid degree of 0.5. Its abstract announces availability while checklist item 5 promises a future release, leaving actual availability unresolved within the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including MPAF, AFLGuard, FedReDefense and recent FL attack/defense work. It removes the dynamic-backdoor citation and associated comparison concerning trigger locations. The central novelty claim and positioning relative to training-phase defenses remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, method and results narratives are extensively condensed and rewritten. Theory and substantial experimental and discussion material move into reorganized appendices A–J, while comparison methods and ablations gain separate subsections and a NeurIPS checklist is added.

P2.justification: v1's sensitivity tables become v2 Figures 3 and 7, and adaptive-attack Table 11 becomes Figure 4. v1 Figures 2–3 are merged into v2 Figure 2, main comparison tables are transposed and compressed, and numerous displays are relocated within a substantially redesigned layout.

improvement.justification: Added implementation details and condensed organization are useful, but v2 removes an aggregation robustness analysis and the checkpoint-privacy caveat. Figure 4 introduces an FNR inconsistent with the retained accuracy and false-positive rate, while Section 5.3's low-error summary conflicts with Table 2's retained 10% and 12.5% FNRs. These accuracy and completeness losses outweigh the limited documentation gains.
